# Explicit CD entries

`cd_entries_mathjax_3_2_2.json` retains 1,060 complete original SVG strings
from D2's frozen MathJax 3.2.2 bundle at upstream commit
`ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee`. The three original asset hashes
are recorded in the fixture and verified by the generator. Each reference
uses a fresh VM with D2's original setup, `em=16`, `ex=8`, no font cache, and
the recorded display mode. No reference is generated by Go.

The primary source is
[`BaseMethods.Entry`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/base/BaseMethods.ts),
[`ArrayItem.checkItem`, `EndEntry`, and `clearEnv`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/base/BaseItems.ts),
[`BraketItem.checkItem`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/braket/BraketItems.ts),
and [`AmsCdMethods.arrow` and `cell`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/amscd/AmsCdMethods.ts).

An actual `&` token emits a closing Entry item. It reduces pending functions,
styles, positions, primes, negations, dots, and fractions before ArrayItem
creates the cell, retains even an empty explicit cell, and clears its lexical
environment. A single Braket first receives any finalized pending MML item;
a braced Braket, ordinary group, or fence owns its own boundary. Commands such
as `\text&` consume the ampersand as an argument and never emit Entry. The CD
parser therefore stops on an actual parser event rather than pre-splitting
raw ampersands. Explicit Entry does not call the CD-specific strut helper.

CD starts with ArrayItem's empty lexical environment and clears it after each
cell. Fonts, identifier patterns, and root-index state cannot leak from the
surrounding expression or a previous cell. User macro definitions and the
logical global stack state remain shared. Cell token scopes are marked as
resolved so an enclosing MathFont post-pass respects that source boundary.

There are 937 byte-exact references: 905 valid renderings and 32 error
controls. Against baseline `c0a304b7ff0fc538d9ca824ca74d421961322d96`, 883
fail and 54 already match. Another 123 references explicitly test Go's safe
XML attribute escaping: 114 errors contain the original raw ampersand in
`data-mjx-error`, and nine valid outputs use raw ampersands in color or tag
attributes. These raw original SVGs remain unchanged in the fixture. The
test permits only four literal attribute replacements, validates candidate
XML, and requires every other byte, including rendered text, to agree. These
qualified comparisons are not counted as byte-exact parity.

The corpus covers leading, trailing, repeated, and empty entries; entries
adjacent to every CD arrow form; object and arrow rows; pending parser items;
font, color, and root-index scope; nested matrices and CD diagrams; escaped
ampersands; comments; child arguments; single and braced Braket/Set owners;
and public macro registration controls. D2's frozen configuration does not
register `\newcommand`, `\def`, or `\let`; these remain original error controls.
Supported operator and paired-delimiter declarations exercise expansion and
argument ownership without enabling packages absent from D2.

The 56 other observations from the complete, deduplicated 1,116-input audit
are preserved in `cd_entries_residuals.json` with raw original, baseline, and
candidate outputs. None was previously byte-exact. They comprise 36 cases
for the independently missing HFill handler/cell alignment and 20 existing
raw CD `@`, row, or environment-ending ownership cases involving empty
Braket/Set or AutoOpen items (44 valid inputs and 12 diagnostic differences).
They are reported separately, not accepted as Go-generated goldens.

A minimal visible witness is `\begin{CD}A&B\end{CD}`. A diagram that also
shows explicit entries interacting with horizontal and vertical arrows is
`\begin{CD}A&@>f>>B\\@VgVV&@VVhV\\C&@>>k>D\end{CD}`.

Regenerate every original reference, including residual originals, with
`node --jitless testdata/generate_cd_entries.cjs PINNED_ASSETS`.
The checked-in inventory is fixed; the generator never filters cases using
candidate output. Workers process batches of 24 fresh VMs. Run
`go test ./... -run 'TestCD(Entry|Finalization)References'` to check these
references and the earlier 1,813 CD finalization references together.

The subsequent HFill implementation now covers all 36 historical HFill
observations as exact original references in `hfill_mathjax_3_2_2.json`.
The historical residual receipt file remains unchanged; the other 20 raw
CD boundary observations remain separate follow-ups.
